summary: Reviewed 5 files (LibraryOptions.cs, FfmpegRunner.cs, SettingsViewModel.cs, SettingsView.axaml, FfmpegRunnerTests.cs). 0 Critical, 0 High findings. Security sign-off: PASS. The most security-relevant surface is FfmpegRunner.ExtractFrameAsync — it correctly uses ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList (array-based argument passing with UseShellExecute=false), which fully mitigates OS command injection. All other OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no blocking issues found. Three Low/Info observations recorded.

comments.note: A03 — Injection (MITIGATED): FfmpegRunner.ExtractFrameAsync (FfmpegRunner.cs lines 58–78) uses ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList.Add() with UseShellExecute=false. This passes arguments directly to the OS without shell interpretation, which fully prevents command injection regardless of the content of videoPath, outputPath, or timecode. Pattern is correct and safe.

A03 — Injection (INFO): FfmpegRunner.ResolveBinaryPath() (FfmpegRunner.cs line 101) returns the user-configured Library.FfmpegPath directly as the process executable. In a local desktop application, the user who configures the path is the same user who owns the machine. This is by design and presents no escalation risk. No remediation required.

A04 — Insecure Design (INFO): LibraryOptions.FfmpegPath (LibraryOptions.cs line 22) and the corresponding SettingsViewModel.FfmpegOverridePath (SettingsViewModel.cs line 42) accept any string without path validation. If the path does not exist or is not executable, Process.Start will throw an InvalidOperationException at runtime, which is caught upstream. For a desktop tool this is acceptable, but a lightweight File.Exists check before launch could improve UX and harden against misconfiguration. Low priority.

A05 — Security Misconfiguration (INFO): FfmpegRunner.ExtractFrameAsync (FfmpegRunner.cs line 94) forwards the raw ffmpeg stderr output as an exception message that is subsequently logged via LogWarning. For a single-user desktop application this is acceptable — the user sees their own process errors. No cross-user information leakage risk exists in this context.

summary: Reviewed 6 files: LibraryOptions.cs, FfmpegRunner.cs, SettingsViewModel.cs, SettingsView.axaml, FfmpegRunnerTests.cs, and api-surface.md. No blocking issues found. All 6 ACs confirmed met. Implementation is well-structured, follows established project patterns, and introduces correct priority semantics (user override → provisioner → PATH). The three-step resolution chain in FfmpegRunner is clearly documented and correctly implemented. SettingsViewModel wiring uses idiomatic record `with {}` mutation. Test coverage addresses all three resolution steps with clear, descriptive names. One cross-cutting architectural concern noted (FfprobeRunner priority inversion vs FfmpegRunner) — logged as project-level comment for future remediation.

comments.note: FfmpegRunner.ResolveBinaryPath() correctly prioritizes user override (Library.FfmpegPath) over provisioner path (ExternalTools.Ffmpeg.FfmpegPath). This is the semantically correct order — an override should always win. The implementation is sound and well-commented.

SettingsViewModel.Save(): Only FfmpegPath is updated within the Library record `with {}` expression, correctly preserving all other Library properties (FfprobePath, RescanExistingFiles). Immutable record mutation pattern is correctly applied.

Pre-existing architectural inconsistency: FfprobeRunner.ResolveBinaryPath() (line 93–97) evaluates ExternalTools.Ffmpeg.FfprobePath (provisioner) BEFORE Library.FfprobePath (user override) — the opposite of FfmpegRunner's correct order. A user who sets Library.FfprobePath expecting it to override the provisioner will be surprised. WP-005 introduced the correct order for FfmpegRunner; FfprobeRunner should be remediated in a follow-up WP to align both runners.

SettingsViewModelTests.cs: No round-trip test for FfmpegOverridePath (PopulateFromSettings → Save → FfmpegOverridePath round-trip). Flagged by Developer and QA. Not a WP-005 AC, but should be added before this area is extended further.

When FfprobeRunner is remediated, update api-surface.md to document both chains consistently.
